The image shows numerous small, angular, dark reddish-brown spots on a plant leaf. As the spots become more dense, the surrounding leaf tissue turns yellow. This matches the description of Brown Spot, which states, "Angular, red to brown spots appear on leaves that vary from tiny specks to quarter-inch diameter, causing affected leaves to turn yellow and fall to the ground." The description also mentions that initial symptoms are "small dark brown spots (less than 1/8 inch) that appear first on lower leaves and progress upward," which is consistent with the visual evidence. While other diseases cause spots, the specific combination of angular, red-to-brown spots leading to widespread yellowing is most characteristic of Brown Spot.
